ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The phrase places the enormous Mount Sumeru inside a tiny mustard seed.
EvidenceBody: Jiangzhou prefect Li Bo explicitly utters the question in three recensions of his exchange with Guizong Zhichang; those witnesses are one case, not three independent deployments. A separate monastic question in the Patriarchs’ Hall Collection asks the same formula in an independently recorded exchange whose respondent is not identified by this stored cut.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: Chan preserves the size-reversal as a public question posed to Guizong and repeated in later records.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The witnesses do not themselves gloss the phrase as unobstructed inclusion, and recensions of one exchange do not multiply independent support.

Senses.Explanation: ‘Mount Sumeru enters a mustard seed’ places an enormous mountain inside a tiny seed. Jiangzhou prefect Li Bo explicitly utters the question in three recensions of his exchange with Guizong Zhichang; those witnesses are one case, not three independent deployments. A separate monastic question in the Patriarchs’ Hall Collection asks the same formula in an independently recorded exchange whose respondent is not identified by this stored cut.
